record.title: The switching-equivalent reconstruction conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same number of vertices. Their decks are **switching equivalent**, written $\mathcal{D}(G) \sim \mathcal{D}(H)$, when there is a bijection between their cards sending each card to a switching-equivalent graph. A switching-equivalent class is **reconstructible** if $\mathcal{D}(G) \sim \mathcal{D}(H)$ implies $G$ belongs to the switching-equivalent class of $H$. **The switching-equivalent reconstruction conjecture.** Every switching-equivalent class on at least $4$ vertices is reconstructible. The paper reports computational verification for representatives with $4\leq n\leq 10$ vertices, but the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Eventual uniqueness of the Erdős extremal set
record.statement:
Let $A(n,k)$ be a set of positive integers not exceeding $n$ from which one cannot select $k+1$ pairwise coprime integers, and let $E(n,k)$ be the set of integers not exceeding $n$ divisible by one of the first $k$ primes.

**Eventual uniqueness conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge3$, there exists an integer $n_k$ such that, for all $n\ge n_k$, if

$$
|A(n,k)|\ge |E(n,k)|,
$$

then

$$
A(n,k)=E(n,k).
$$

This strengthens eventual equality of the extremal size to uniqueness of the extremal set. The paper proves the analogous uniqueness result for $k=4$ and derives this conjecture from its auxiliary shifted-block conjectures.

record.title: Multicolored Erdős matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ be the family of $k$-element subsets of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{F}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{F}_t$ be families of such subsets. A rainbow matching of size $t$ is a collection of $t$ pairwise disjoint edges containing exactly one edge from each family. **Multicolored Erdős matching conjecture.** If

$$
|\mathcal{F}_i|>\max\left\{\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-t+1}{k},\binom{kt-1}{k}\right\}
$$

for every $1\leq i\leq t$, then there is a rainbow matching of size $t$. This is a multicolored strengthening of Erdős's matching conjecture, considered independently by Aharoni and Howard. The source presents it as a conjectural statement; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Thomassen's connected partition conjecture with cross-degree condition
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A graph is **$r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves it connected; for a vertex set $M\subseteq V(G)$, the condition that each vertex in $V_1$ has at least $k$ neighbours in $V_2$ is a cross-degree condition.

**Thomassen's partition conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists $f(k)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that if $G$ is an $f(k)$-connected graph and $M\subseteq V(G)$ consists of $k$ vertices, then there exists a partition $V_1,V_2$ of $V(G)$ such that $M\subseteq V_1$, both $G[V_1]$ and $G[V_2]$ are $k$-connected, and each vertex in $V_1$ has at least $k$ neighbours in $V_2$.

The source calls this a conjecture of Thomassen and explains that the graph version of the preceding tournament subdivision theorem would follow from it. Its resolution is not supplied in the paper.

record.title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for hereditary graph classes
record.statement:
A graph $H$ is an induced subgraph of a graph $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by removing vertices. A class of graphs is **hereditary** if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs and under isomorphism, and it is **proper** if it is not the class of all graphs. A hereditary class has the **Erdős–Hajnal property** if there exists $c>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph in the class contains a clique or a stable set of size at least $n^c$.

**Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** Every proper hereditary class of graphs has the Erdős–Hajnal property.

Equivalently, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs with no induced copy of $H$ should contain a clique or stable set of polynomial size in the number of vertices. The conjecture is a strengthening of Ramsey's theorem; the paper notes that it has been proved for graphs of bounded VC-dimension, while the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Clonal Ding–Oporowski–Oxley–Vertigan-type minor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $M$ be a $3$-connected clonal matroid. The matroids $U_{2,2m}$ and $U_{2m-2,2m}$ are uniform matroids, while $\Lambda_m$ and $\Delta_m$ denote the named matroids used in the source. **Clonal minor conjecture.** There is a function $f(m)$ such that, if $M$ has at least $f(m)$ elements, then $M$ has one of the following as a clonal minor: $U_{2,2m}$, $U_{2m-2,2m}$, $\Lambda_m$, or $\Delta_m$.

record.title: The Edge Reconstruction Conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, its **edge deck** is the multiset of unlabeled graphs $\{G-e:e\in E(G)\}$. A graph $G$ is **edge reconstructible** if every graph with the same edge deck is isomorphic to $G$.

**The Edge Reconstruction Conjecture.** Every graph with at least four edges is edge reconstructible.

The source presents this as one of the oldest unsolved problems in graph theory and studies computational generation of sparse $2$-connected graphs as an application. The conjecture remains open in the supplied context.

record.title: Algebraic form of the Kelly–Ulam vertex-reconstruction conjecture
record.statement: Let $V=\{1,\ldots,f\}$, let $E$ be the set of two-element subsets of $V$, and let $\mathcal{G}_f$ be the quotient of the real polynomial algebra in variables $x_{\{i,j\}}$ by the relations $x_{\{i,j\}}^2=x_{\{i,j\}}$. For each graph isomorphism class $[G]$, let $p_{[G]}$ be the corresponding invariant orbit sum, and let $\mathcal{I}_f$ be the set of polynomials $p_{[G]}$ for graphs $G$ with at least one isolated vertex. **Algebraic form of the Kelly–Ulam conjecture.** If $f$ is at least three, then the subalgebra of $\mathcal{G}_f$ generated by the polynomials of $\mathcal{I}_f$ is $\mathcal{G}_f$ itself. The source states that this is equivalent to the vertex-reconstruction conjecture, because these polynomials encode the numbers of subgraphs appearing in the vertex-deleted subgraphs.

record.title: The reconstruction conjecture for finite simple graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph. For each vertex $v\in V(G)$, let $G_v=[G-v]_{\cong}$ be its **card**, and let

$$
\mathcal{D}(G)=\{\!\{G_v:v\in V(G)\}\!\}
$$

be its **deck**. The graph $G$ is **reconstructible** if every graph $H$ with $\mathcal{D}(H)=\mathcal{D}(G)$ is isomorphic to $G$. **The reconstruction conjecture.** Every graph of order at least $3$ is reconstructible. This is one of the central open problems in structural graph theory, asserting that a graph is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of its vertex-deleted induced subgraphs. The conjecture remains wide open, although the paper proves it for interval graphs with at least three vertices.

record.title: Seymour's image-size conjecture for finite reflexive relations
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite reflexive relation, and let $j$ be an integer. Write $\Gamma^j(x)$ for the $j$-fold image of $x$ and $\Gamma^{-1}(x)$ for its inverse image. **Seymour's conjecture.** There is an $x\in V$ such that at least one of the following holds:

$$
|\Gamma^j(x)|\ge 1+j(|\Gamma(x)|-1),
$$

or

$$
\Gamma^{-1}(x)\cap\Gamma^j(x)\neq\{x\}.
$$

This is a relation-theoretic formulation of Seymour's directed-cycle conjecture. The paper proves the asserted growth alternative for point-symmetric relations under suitable hypotheses, while the general conjecture is presented as open.

record.title: Graham's tree reconstruction conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple undirected graph. A **tree** is an acyclic, connected graph. Its **line graph** $L(G)$ has vertex set $E$, with distinct $e,f\nin E$ adjacent exactly when $e$ and $f$ are incident in $G$. Define the iterated line graphs by

$$
L^{(0)}(G)=G,
$$

and

$$
L^{(j+1)}(G)=L(L^{(j)}(G))\qquad (j\geq 1).
$$

**Graham's tree reconstruction conjecture.** For each sequence of natural numbers $a_0,a_1,a_2,\ldots$, all the conditions $|L^{(j)}(G)|=a_j$ for $j\geq 0$ are satisfied by at most one tree $G$.

The conjecture asks whether the sequence of sizes of a tree and all its iterated line graphs uniquely determines the tree. Apart from a few simple observations, little is known; the paper gives lower bounds on the number of trees distinguishable by these sequences but does not resolve the conjecture.

record.title: Gowers inverse conjecture for the Boolean cube
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 1$ and let $\varepsilon>0$. For each $n\geq 1$, write $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ for the Boolean vector space, let $f:\mathbf{F}_2^n\to[-1,1]$, let $\|f\|_{U^d(\mathbf{F}_2^n)}$ denote its Gowers uniformity norm, and let $S_{d-1}(\mathbf{F}_2^n)$ be the set of Reed–Muller codes of order at most $d-1$. **Gowers inverse conjecture.** If $\|f\|_{U^d(\mathbf{F}_2^n)}\geq\varepsilon$, then there exists a constant $\delta>0$, depending only on $d$ and $\varepsilon$, and a code $g\in S_{d-1}(\mathbf{F}_2^n)$ such that

$$
|\langle f,g\rangle_{L^2(\mathbf{F}_2^n)}|\geq\delta.
$$

Thus, a function with large $U^d$ norm should have nontrivial correlation with a Reed–Muller code of order at most $d-1$. The conjecture describes the structured objects detected by the Gowers norm on $\mathbf{F}_2^n$; it is known in low-degree cases, while the conjecture for $d>3$ remains open because of the large number of relevant Reed–Muller codes and the resulting lack of Fourier-type orthogonality.

record.title: The Duchet–Maffray–Woodall product conjecture for independent sets and complete minors
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\alpha(G)$ for its independence number, the maximum size of an independent set, and let $h(G)$ be the size of a largest complete minor of $G$. **Duchet–Maffray–Woodall product conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\alpha(G)h(G)\geq |V(G)|.
$$

This conjecture follows from Hadwiger's conjecture, since $\alpha(G)\chi(G)\geq |V(G)|$. It was observed independently by Duchet and Maffray and by Woodall, and its general status is not resolved here.

record.title: Zhang et al.'s conjecture on adjacent vertex distinguishing total colourings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\chi_{at}(G)$ denote its adjacent vertex distinguishing total chromatic number, the least number of colours in a proper total colouring such that every pair of adjacent vertices has a different set of colours appearing on the vertex and its incident edges. **Zhang et al.'s conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\chi_{at}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+3.
$$

The conjecture seeks a sharp general upper bound for adjacent vertex distinguishing total colourings. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: The list coloring conjecture for line graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **choice number** $ch(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that every assignment of a $k$-element list of colors to each vertex admits a proper coloring from the assigned lists. Its **list chromatic index** is $ch'(G)=ch(L(G))$, where $L(G)$ is the line graph of $G$, and let $\chi'(G)$ be the chromatic index. **List coloring conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
ch'(G)=\chi'(G).
$$

The conjecture says that line graphs have no gap between list chromatic index and chromatic index; no resolution status is supplied in the source span.

record.title: Equality of group and group-list edge chromatic numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. Denote its group edge chromatic number by $\chi'_g(G)$ and its group list edge chromatic number by $\chi'_{gl}(G)$. **Equality conjecture.** For every simple graph $G$,

$$
\chi'_g(G)=\chi'_{gl}(G).
$$

This is presented alongside the proposed analogue of Vizing's theorem as a conjecture about the coincidence of group edge choice parameters. The supplied status evidence marks the candidate as resolved, but gives no identifying theorem or reference.

record.title: Alavi–Erdős–Malde–Schwenk conjecture on unimodality for trees and forests
record.statement: A tree is a connected acyclic graph, and a forest is an acyclic graph. For a graph $G$, its independence sequence $(i_0(G),i_1(G),\ldots,i_{\alpha(G)}(G))$ records the numbers of independent sets of each cardinality. **Alavi–Erdős–Malde–Schwenk conjecture.** Every tree and every forest has a unimodal independence sequence. The paper states that this conjecture remains open, in contrast with the disproved unimodality conjecture for all well-covered graphs.

record.title: Linear Hadwiger's conjecture
record.statement: Let $K_t$ be the complete graph on $t$ vertices, and call a graph $K_t$-minor-free if it has no $K_t$ minor. A graph is $k$-colourable if it has a proper colouring using at most $k$ colours. **Linear Hadwiger's conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every integer $t\geqslant1$, every $K_t$-minor-free graph is $Ct$-colourable. This is a natural weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture. The best known general upper bounds are superlinear, so the conjecture remains open.
